record.context_brief: Virtual classes and tautological cohomology on moduli of curves
record.original_question: Let X be a nonsingular projective variety over C, let M_g(X, β) be the moduli space of stable maps to X in curve class β, and let π: M_g(X, β) → M_g be the morphism that forgets the map and remembers only the domain curve. The moduli space M_g(X, β) carries a virtual fundamental class [M_g(X, β)]^vir. Does the pushed-forward class π_*[M_g(X, β)]^vir in the cohomology H_*(M_g) always lie in the tautological ring of M_g?

evidence.quote: Let X be a nonsingular, projective variety over C. Let Mg(X, β) be the moduli space of stable maps and let π : Mg(X, β) → Mg be the forgetful morphism
Q1. Does π∗[Mg(X, β)]vir ∈ H∗(Mg) lie in the tautological ring in cohomology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a nonsingular projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$, let $\beta \in H_2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ be a curve class, and let $g \geq 2$. Denote by $\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)$ the moduli space of stable maps from genus-$g$ curves to $X$ representing $\beta$, equipped with its virtual fundamental class $[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}}$. Let $\pi : \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) \to \overline{M}_g$ be the forgetful morphism that sends a stable map to (the stabilization of) its domain curve, and let $M_g \subset \overline{M}_g$ denote the open locus of nonsingular curves. The tautological ring $R^*(M_g) \subset H^*(M_g,\mathbb{Q})$ is the subring generated by the kappa classes $\kappa_i$, and one defines the homological tautological subring of $H_*(M_g,\mathbb{Q})$ via Poincaré duality.

Question: Does the restriction to $M_g$ of the pushforward $\pi_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}} \in H_*(M_g,\mathbb{Q})$ always lie in the tautological subring, for every choice of $X$ and $\beta$?
artifact.category_tag: Tautological ring of moduli of curves
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known speculation (the "Cohomology Speculation" of Pandharipande and collaborators). It remains open in general, but substantial partial results are known: tautologicality has been established for relative Gromov–Witten pushforwards in various settings, for smooth complete intersections in products of projective spaces and in toric varieties (with ambient insertions), and for varieties admitting flat proper morphisms to a curve with simple-normal-crossing singular fibers. No counterexample is known and the full statement is not proved.

status_evidence.title: Tautological relations for stable maps to a target variety
status_evidence.snippet: Studies tautological relations from stable maps to a target variety, providing partial evidence for the conjecture that pushforwards of virtual classes are tautological.
status_evidence.claim: Significant partial results are known toward the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Relative maps and tautological classes (Faber–Pandharipande)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that pushforwards of relative Gromov–Witten classes are tautological in important cases.
status_evidence.claim: Tautologicality is known in the relative setting and in further special cases.

status_evidence.title: Gromov-Witten theory, degenerations, and the tautological ring (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Cohomology Speculation and Chow Speculation and recent progress for complete intersections and degenerations to SNC fibers.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains open in general but recent work provides strong evidence.
